currentContext.strengths: Deep, long-standing OEM relationships across leading 2W and 4W manufacturers (Yamaha, Suzuki, TVS, Honda, Royal Enfield, Hero, Mahindra & Mahindra, Daimler India, Kubota, Hyundai) evidenced by multiple annual cost/quality/delivery awards|In-house R&D and validation infrastructure - NABL-accredited photometric laboratory, EMI/EMC testing lab, environmental/vibration/salt-spray chambers - reducing dependence on external testing and accelerating product development|Backward-integrated manufacturing across moulding (injection/2K/3K moulding up to 1300T), electronics (SMT, robotic soldering) and tooling|Technology partnerships/technical assistance agreements with Japanese majors - Aisan Industry Co., Ltd. and Toyodenso Co., Ltd. / Toyota Tsusho Corp.|Global design/R&D footprint through wholly-owned subsidiaries in Japan and Italy and a Hong Kong JV, supporting international OEM and premium European car programs
currentContext.strategies: Vision to be a dominant player in automotive lighting by developing innovative technologies, and to build a trusted, safe, self-reliant and sustainable global organisation.|Continue investing ahead of the curve - strengthening technological capabilities, expanding manufacturing infrastructure and developing innovative products to create lasting customer value.|Growth strategy to be supported by strong internal accruals, prudent capital allocation and a healthy balance sheet, pursuing growth with financial discipline and long-term sustainability.|Grow the four-wheeler business as an important pillar of long-term growth strategy, building on the newly commenced supply relationship with Mahindra & Mahindra and a growing PV customer base.|Build in-house electronics design, validation and testing capability (EMI/EMC lab) to strengthen engineering depth, speed up product development and reduce dependence on external testing facilities.|Pursue a green-energy/sustainability journey (rooftop solar and open-access renewable power across plants) in support of a long-term carbon-neutral objective.|Mission to be market leader across products through global competitiveness, with a customer-focused approach to safety, quality, cost and on-time delivery.|Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (adopted 30 June 2021 pursuant to SEBI Listing Regulation 43A, applicable as the Company is among the top 1000 listed entities by market capitalisation) guides recommendation/declaration of interim and final dividends based on financial parameters and internal/external factors, and how retained earnings are utilised. The Company states it has been consistently declaring higher dividends every year since listing. Broader growth strategy is stated to be supported by strong internal accruals, prudent capital allocation and a healthy balance sheet, pursuing growth with financial discipline and long-term sustainability.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26 the Company commissioned and inaugurated a new state-of-the-art EMI/EMC Testing Laboratory at its R&D-Electronics, Innovation Centre & Corporate Office in Gurugram, to enable in-house EMI/EMC validation of automotive lighting products for two-wheelers and four-wheelers, strengthen backward integration in engineering/validation infrastructure and reduce dependence on external testing facilities. In parallel, the Company began a green-energy rollout - rooftop solar and open-access renewable power - starting at its Hosur plant (~65% of energy needs via open-access solar, with a further ~20% being added via wind energy), with similar initiatives being progressively extended to other manufacturing locations. Separately, reinstatement is under way at the fire-damaged Tapukara Unit-VIII (fire of 23 August 2025): undamaged Ground Floor/Basement production resumed on 29 August 2025, while as an interim measure production set-up for Bank Angle Sensor (BAS) and 4-Wheeler (especially Mahindra & Mahindra) parts was reinstated at the Rai Plant (Unit-VII) and restarted in September 2025; full building/machinery reinstatement at Tapukara continues. The Rai Plant's own re-instatement (from the June 2023 fire) was completed during the year, with the insurance claim assessment in its final stages.

risks.note: The Company supplies Rear View Mirrors to almost all of its OEM customers (predominantly two-wheeler) and is the sole supplier for several valued OEM customers' Rear View Mirror requirements - making performance sensitive to those OEMs' own programme volumes and sourcing decisions.

MD&A explicitly flags the automotive industry's rapidly evolving environment - changing customer preferences, technological advancements, geopolitical developments, supply chain disruptions, regulatory changes and macroeconomic uncertainties - as an ongoing risk requiring organisational resilience and agility.
The Company's Enterprise Risk Management framework explicitly names cybersecurity risk arising from increasing digitalisation of business processes as a monitored risk category.

risks.risk: Natural calamities and physical-asset risk (fire, theft, accidents)
risks.note: ERM framework explicitly covers natural calamities that may disrupt manufacturing operations, and risks to the safety/security of employees, assets and infrastructure including fire, theft, accidents and other unforeseen events, addressed via preventive measures, protocols and periodic reviews.
The Board-approved Risk Management Policy explicitly names foreign currency exchange rate risk as one of the risk categories covered by the Company's enterprise risk management framework.
The Risk Management Policy names market risk as one of the categories the framework is designed to identify, mitigate and monitor, alongside cyber, forex and natural-calamity risk.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Fiem Industries manufactures Automotive Lights, signaling equipment and parts, Rear View Mirrors and Parts, and Plastic Moulded Parts, sold predominantly to automobile OEMs and aftermarket dealers. LED lighting now accounts for 63% of the automotive lighting business (up from 59% last year), and the company is expanding its four-wheeler presence alongside its established two-wheeler OEM base.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Two-wheeler segment expected to remain central to India's mobility landscape given its affordability, utility and deep relevance across urban, semi-urban and rural markets.
- Premiumisation, connected features, safety regulations and electric mobility are steadily reshaping customer expectations and product architecture across vehicle categories.
- For automotive lighting specifically, the transition from conventional lighting to LED, projector lamps, DRLs, ambient lighting, adaptive and intelligent lighting systems is increasing the value content of lighting per vehicle.
- Rising safety awareness, stricter regulatory expectations, premiumisation of two-wheelers/passenger vehicles and increasing OEM design differentiation are expected to support demand for advanced lighting products.
- Companies with strong design capabilities, engineering depth, cost competitiveness and close OEM relationships are expected to remain better positioned in this evolving environment.
- Auto component industry expected to be a key beneficiary of OEM localisation, supply-chain resilience, cost optimisation and technology partnerships, across both domestic and export markets.
- Electrification remains one of the most important long-term industry themes, with electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler segments seen as early beneficiaries of policy support and expanding product availability.
- Growing vehicle complexity - higher electronic content, LED lighting systems, sensors, controllers, wiring and thermal management - expected to create new avenues for value-added component manufacturing.
- Structural domestic demand drivers cited: low vehicle penetration versus developed markets, rising disposable incomes, urbanisation, improved financing availability and higher replacement demand.
- Four-wheeler business described as supported by 'a growing customer base and a healthy order pipeline', with management confident of strengthening its position in this high-value segment.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved to 13.93% (from 13.21% YoY) due to operating leverage (capacity utilization ~80%), higher LED mix, and in-house SMT/assembly localization (only LED chips imported); no raw material cost pressure cited

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Capex prioritized for growth (INR100cr FY26); no dividend or buyback mentioned; no debt used; focus on internal funding and organic expansion

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26 the Company commissioned and inaugurated a new state-of-the-art EMI/EMC Testing Laboratory at its R&D-Electronics, Innovation Centre & Corporate Office in Gurugram, to enable in-house EMI/EMC validation of automotive lighting products for two-wheelers and four-wheelers, strengthen backward integration in engineering/validation infrastructure and reduce dependence on external testing facilities. In parallel, the Company began a green-energy rollout - rooftop solar and open-access renewable power - starting at its Hosur plant (~65% of energy needs via open-access solar, with a further ~20% being added via wind energy), with similar initiatives being progressively extended to other manufacturing locations. Separately, reinstatement is under way at the fire-damaged Tapukara Unit-VIII (fire of 23 August 2025): undamaged Ground Floor/Basement production resumed on 29 August 2025, while as an interim measure production set-up for Bank Angle Sensor (BAS) and 4-Wheeler (especially Mahindra & Mahindra) parts was reinstated at the Rai Plant (Unit-VII) and restarted in September 2025; full building/machinery reinstatement at Tapukara continues. The Rai Plant's own re-instatement (from the June 2023 fire) was completed during the year, with the insurance claim assessment in its final stages.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Deep, long-standing OEM relationships across leading 2W and 4W manufacturers (Yamaha, Suzuki, TVS, Honda, Royal Enfield, Hero, Mahindra & Mahindra, Daimler India, Kubota, Hyundai) evidenced by multiple annual cost/quality/delivery awards
- In-house R&D and validation infrastructure - NABL-accredited photometric laboratory, EMI/EMC testing lab, environmental/vibration/salt-spray chambers - reducing dependence on external testing and accelerating product development
- Backward-integrated manufacturing across moulding (injection/2K/3K moulding up to 1300T), electronics (SMT, robotic soldering) and tooling
- Technology partnerships/technical assistance agreements with Japanese majors - Aisan Industry Co., Ltd. and Toyodenso Co., Ltd. / Toyota Tsusho Corp.
- Global design/R&D footprint through wholly-owned subsidiaries in Japan and Italy and a Hong Kong JV, supporting international OEM and premium European car programs

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leadership transition] With effect from June 01, 2026, founder Mr. J.K. Jain was re-designated Executive Chairman (from Chairman & Managing Director), Mr. Rahul Jain was elevated to Managing Director, and Ms. Aanchal Jain was re-designated Joint Managing Director; Mr. Rajesh Sharma continues as Joint Managing Director and Mr. Kashi Ram Yadav as Whole-time Director.
- [Bonus issue] FY22 and FY23 EPS figures in both the consolidated and standalone income statements, and several per-share charts, are footnoted RESTATED ON POST-BONUS SHARE CAPITAL BASIS.
- [Group structure] Wholly-owned subsidiaries are Fiem Industries Japan Co., Ltd. (Japan) and Fiem Research and Technology s.r.l (Italy); the JV company is Fiem Kyowa (HK) Mould Company Limited (Hong Kong), a 50:50 JV set up in 2017 with KYOWA Co., Ltd., Japan for high-class moulds and tools.
- [Fuel pump JV] In 2018 FIEM entered a Joint Venture with Aisan Industry Co. Ltd., Japan and Toyota Tsusho India Pvt. Ltd. for manufacture of Fuel Pump Module for the Indian market.
- [Regulatory approvals] The Integrated Passenger Information System with LED Display (IPIS) holds approval from the Ministry of Railways - Research Design and Standard Organization (RDSO) for train indication, coach guidance and PC-based announcement, and the Association of State Road Transport Undertakings inspected the LED based Destination system and found it satisfactory.
